title: Lavorano per Guess, Calvin Klein, e Tommy Hilfiger, ma guadagnano meno di 1 dollaro al giorno
description: Il settore tessile in Etiopia – il secondo paese più popoloso dell’Africa con 105 milioni di abitanti - cresce a ritmi significativi. Il governo prevede che le esportazioni del comparto, che attualmente valgono 145 milioni di dollari l'anno, salgano a circa 30 miliardi. Un obiettivo tuttavia che appare irrealistico, se non altro perché bassi salari hanno portato a una scarsa produttività, a ripetuti scioperi e a un esasperato turn over (le fabbriche sostituiscono in media tutti i loro dipendenti ogni dodici mesi). Secondo un rapporto della New York University, i lavoratori etiopi con 26 dollari al mese sono tra i meno retribuiti al mondo. E, paradossalmente, sono dipendenti di marchi globali come Guess, H&M, Calvin Klein, Gap, Tommy Hilfiger, e JC Penney che nel paese africano hanno delocalizzato i loro stabilimenti. L'Etiopia, che mira a diventare il principale centro manifatturiero del continente, ha sedotto gli investitori facendo passare il messaggio che sarebbe stato sufficiente riconoscere ai lavoratori meno di un terzo dei salari offerti in Bangladesh. E si consideri che per lo stesso lavoro i kenyoti sono pagati 207 dollari al mese e i cinesi 326.

description: Zakup gry erotycznej to krok w kierunku pozytywnej zmiany sypialnianego repertuaru. Wiele nietuzinkowych zestawów gier dla par znajduje się na stronie swiat-doznan.pl. Możliwość zapoznania się z różnymi formami i scenariuszami pozwala na dobór idealnego rozwiązania, które z pewnością rozpali atmosferę w łóżku.Zanim dwie osoby w pełni odkryją swoje potrzeby seksualne, zwykle mija dużo czasu. Z kolei nieznajomość wzajemnych pragnień może determinować mniejszą satysfakcję z erotycznych doznań. Implementacja gier erotycznych to rozwiązanie dla osób, które chcą wprowadzić ciekawy, nietuzinkowy element rozrywki do swojej łóżkowej rutyny. To właśnie te aspekty warunkują cenę poszczególnych produktów. W sklepie swiat-doznan.pl dostępne są nietuzinkowe, różnorodne zestawy, które pozwalają na odkrywcze aktywności w sferze intymnej. Implementacja gry erotycznej w swoim łóżkowym rytuale to doskonały sposób na rozpoczęcie szalonej przygody z seksem analnym czy poznanie praktyki BDSM w zupełnie inny sposób.jesteśmy bardzo zadowoleni z zestawu, który zakupiliśmy z partnerką w sklepie swiat-doznan.pl. jest to doskonały pomysł na urozmaicenie sfery seksualnej i znalezienie ciekawych pomysłów na grę wstępną. duży plus za to, że produkt dotarł do nas dyskretnie zapakowany. polecankoBartoszPolecam każdej parze, która chce, wprowadzić element pikanterii do swojego intymnego rytuału. Często dodajemy do scenariusza coś od siebie, często improwizujemy. Armut, Nahrungsmittelknappheit, häufige Überschwemmungen. Viele Menschen können nicht lesen oder schreiben, sind nicht in die moderne Ökonomie eingebunden und haben nur unzureichenden Zugang zu medizinischer Versorgung. In Äthiopien sterben heute noch immer 353 Frauen auf 100.000 Lebendgeburten. title: SCS Project Health Program Supply Chain Advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB
description: Main Purpose Of Job The Health Program Supply Chain advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB, embedded within the Ministry of Health’s Pharmaceutical and Medical Devices Lead Executive Office (PMD LEO), provides technical assistance in demand planning, resource mobilization, procurement, stock status and pipeline monitoring, and overall supply chain management of HIV/AIDS and TB program commodities. The role is designed to strengthen MOH PMD-LEO systems and is delivered under the leadership and direction of the PMD-LEO, with the explicit objective of progressively and fully transitioning responsibilities, knowledge, and support to the MOH PMD‑LEO. The Advisor works closely with MOH HIV and TB Health programs and Finance Chief Executive Office of MOH, and Ethiopian Pharmaceutical Supply Service (EPSS), to strengthen an efficient, responsive, and sustainable supply chain system for HIV/AIDS and TB products. The role focuses on improving supply chain performance through process optimization to minimize wastage, reduce costs, and enhance operational efficiency. The Advisor ensures effective inventory management, storage, distribution, and quality assurance of HIV/AIDS and TB commodities, strengthening program specific and supply chain coordination platforms, and supporting public and private sector counterparts in strengthening supply chain operations. By promoting data driven decision- making and alignment with national health program priorities, the Advisor contributes to a sustainable and resilient health supply chain system, ultimately improving access to lifesaving HIV/AIDS and TB commodities. In addition, the advisor plays a key role in capacity building efforts through technical mentorship, coaching, knowledge and skill transfer to MoH and EPSS teams to enhance long-term supply chain management capacity. Specific Responsibilities Under supervision of the Supply Chain Lead of SCS and the Supply Chain Desk Head of PMD LEO/MOH, and in close collaboration with technical teams in SCS Project and PMD LEO, the Health Program Supply Chain Advisor for HIV/AIDS and TB will carry out the following responsibilities: Provide strategic level support in developing pharmaceutical supply chain strategies, projects, and action plans while advising MoH and EPSS leadership on initiatives to enhance HIV/AIDS and TB supply chain efficiency and effectiveness. Collaborate with MoH key functions, EPSS, USG SC Project HIV and TB Supply Chain Manager as well as Forecasting and Supply Plan Manager, and other partners to strengthen the HIV/AIDS and TB commodities supply chain, ensuring accurate quantification, timely procurement, and continuous availability of required commodities across all levels of the supply chain system. Provide expert guidance to SCS management and staff on HIV/AIDS and TB-related health policies, strategies, interventions, and innovations. Work with public and private sector partners to implement HIV/AIDS and TB supply chain activities across the country, ensuring alignment with national health program strategies. Collaborate with the SCS team, MOH, EPSS, and other key stakeholders to design and implement supply chain strengthening strategies, tools, and approaches to improve HIV and TB commodity availability while conducting and supporting supply management assessments to evaluate and enhance supply chain operations. Provide technical assistance to MoH, and RHBs in translating national policies into regional and woreda-level implementation guidelines. Compile, evaluate, and maintain an evidence-based HIV/AIDS and TB-related supply chain challenges and best practices to inform advocacy, policy dialogue, and planning efforts with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs), Woreda health Office teams, Health facilities and implementing partners. Collaborate with SCS team, MOH, EPSS, and other key stakeholders to design and implement supply chain strengthening strategies, tools, and approaches to improve HIV/AIDS and TB commodities availability. Under the guidance of the PMD‑LEO Desk Head, serve as a liaison between the MOH, DOS, and SCS to enhance coordination and collaboration and to advance MOH supply chain priorities. Support PMDLEO in advancing overall supply chain maturity through strategic engagement at the MOH level. Strengthen coordination and alignment among MOH, EPSS, EPHI, and EFDA by serving as an effective liaison across these and other relevant stakeholders. Support forecasting and supply planning for HIV/AIDS and TB commodities, including new pediatric formulations, ensuring an uninterrupted supply of HIV/AIDS and TB program products. title: Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9)
description: For Project: Service Contract for Technical Facility Unit (TFU) for the EU Support to Public Finance Management Reforms in Ethiopia (EUSPRE) The European Union is supporting the Government of Ethiopia through the EUSPRE public financial management (PFM) project. The EUSPRE Technical Facility Unit (TFU) provides oversight of the EUSPRE programme and specifically support and capacity building support to the Federal government’s PFM Reforms program. The Overall Objective of the EUSPRE programme is enhanced transparency and efficiency of public financial management for better service delivery and inclusive development . DAI is looking for a Senior Non-Key Expert – IT Audit (SNKE – Audit 9) to Support the Office of the Federal Auditor General (OFAG) by updating the current IT Audit Manual and Working Papers and delivering related Dissemination Workshop and Classroom Training. Scope of work The scope of work for this assignment includes the following activities/ tasks to be undertaken by the NKE, in conjunction with the OFAG designated working group led by the Director of ITAU, which are further detailed in the two sub-sections below: 1. Carry out consultations with the KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU, and assessment of the scope of work. Prepare an Inception Report with a detailed workplan to carry out the entire assignment and deliver the outputs. 2. Review already prepared/approved Gap Analysis related to areas of manual requiring update in conjunction with KE3 (TFU) and the OFAG designated working group led by Director of ITAU. 3. Support updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2018) and respective Working Papers, as agreed during the inception meetings, and in line with the approved changes set within Gap Analysis, taking in consideration necessary customisation to the Ethiopian context. 4. Develop dissemination workshop materials for the updated version of IT Audit Manual and WPs, facilitate and deliver a one-day Dissemination Workshop for the Senior Management (total 40 attendees). The workshop will be a ‘kick-start’ to establish arrangements for adoption and rollout for the updated version of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers. 5. Develop two training modules (materials) for Classroom Trainings on the updated OFAG IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) and new IT Audit practices practical for the ITAU Director and Auditors, FADs and P&ED Directors and Managers, AQAD and T&ED teams members (total 40 participants). 6. Facilitate and deliver training over two one-week training sessions (five days each, total ten days). First week (Module 1) is going to be delivered to 30 participants comprised of staff from ITAU and selected staff from: FADs, P&ED, AQAD and T&ED; while second week (Module 2) is going to be delivered to 10 participants referring to staff from ITAU (total 40 participants). Classroom Trainings will comprise of two training modules (materials) covering following: I. Module 1 will cover a detailed presentation of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026): § An Introduction to updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual & WPs (Version 2026) covering: a. In-depth description and elaboration of the IT Audit Manual content: Introduction, Establishing IT Audit Function, IT Audit Standards, Frameworks and Audit Work, Planning Process, Conducting the Audit, Reporting, Follow-up, Communication, Quality Control. b. In-depth description and elaboration of the WPs content. II. Module 2 will cover practical exercises relating to the application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) using IT Audit Case Study. The case study should cover all of the following topics, as agreed with OFAG Management: § An introduction to new working practices using IT Audit Case Study in form of classroom exercise as part of practical application of updated OFAG’s IT Audit Manual and WPs (Version 2026) in the following areas: Audit of IT Governance and Segregation of Duties; Audit of Network and Systems (Hardware & Software); Audit of Active Directory and other User Management Systems; Audit of IT Security and Cybersecurity Areas; Audit of Data Centres and it’s Environment; Audit of ERP Applications and Databases; Audit of Backup Solutions and Disaster Recovery; Audit of AI and Emerging Technologies (Cloud Computing, IoT, Big Data, etc.); Audit of IT Projects and Systems under Development. 7. Prepare combined end-of-assignment report reflecting on the work delivered for updating of the OFAG IT Audit Manual (Version 2026) and respective Working Papers as well as for delivery of Dissemination Workshop and delivery of Classroom Trainings. Output(s) Deliver Inception Report with a detailed Gantt chart workplan to carry out the assignment and deliver the outputs. title: Digital Identity Lead - Frontier Technologies Foundations
description: The Digital Identity Lead is a high-visibility, dual-engine role sitting at the intersection of technical architecture and commercial origination. The role's anchor specialism is Digital Identity (DID): you will bring deep, hands-on experience of building or implementing national-scale digital identity architectures, and you will ultimately own FT's DID service line. Because identity is a load-bearing foundation beneath the rest of FT's foundations stack — every national data ecosystem depends on a trusted unique identifier, and every identity system depends on a cryptographic trust and security layer — this role is deliberately broader than a pure DID mandate. You will carry contributory technical responsibility into Data at Societal Scale (national data exchange, interoperability, data governance) and Cybersecurity (PKI, cryptographic trust frameworks, Zero Trust design), acting as FT's connective thread across these three foundations. You will not be expected to lead these adjacent domains, but to ensure DID engagements are architected coherently with them, and to lend specialist input when FT's Data and Cyber leads need identity-layer expertise. You will also act as a core business builder for the practice, using your global network within the World Bank, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and the broader DPI ecosystem to originate new projects, secure funding, and scale Genesis's pipeline across all three foundations. 1 | Key Responsibilities 1.1 Business Origination & Strategic Networks (35%) Pipeline Generation: Leverage existing, high-level relationships within the World Bank, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), Co-Develop, and key regional development banks to position Genesis as the premier global choice for DPI implementation — opening doors for Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity mandates as a natural extension of DID relationships Deal Structuring & Capture: Proactively identify, shape, and capture business opportunities across the DID and foundational ID ecosystem; lead high-value proposal development and pitches for donor-funded tenders, and contribute technical input to Data and Cybersecurity pursuits where identity is a component Ecosystem Integration: Act as a primary interface between Genesis and the global identity, data, and digital government communities, aligning firm capabilities with emerging donor strategies, funding cycles, and country-level roadmaps 1.2 Digital Identity — Technical Leadership & Implementation (35%) National-Scale Delivery: Serve as the chief subject-matter expert on the architectural design, governance, and roll-out strategies of foundational or functional national digital ID systems Framework Champion: Embed international standards and best practice — specifically World Bank ID4D principles, ID4Africa frameworks, and open-source stacks such as MOSIP — into localised government roadmaps Next-Gen Identity Architecture: Advise clients on the transition toward Decentralised Identity (DID) ecosystems, Verifiable Credentials (VCs), and self-sovereign identity (SSI) frameworks Cross-Functional Integration: Ensure identity frameworks interoperate seamlessly with the other DPI pillars — payments, data exchange, and (in time) national cybersecurity architecture 1.3 Contributory Technical Leadership: Data & Cybersecurity Foundations (20%) Data at Societal Scale: Advise on how unique identifiers and civil registries underpin national data exchange and interoperability architecture; contribute an identity lens to national data strategy and data governance engagements led by FT's Data practice Cybersecurity: Bring your natural DID-adjacent expertise in cryptographic trust frameworks, PKI, and public/private key infrastructure to inform Zero Trust architecture, authentication and authorisation design, and identity-linked security posture assessments — supporting the build-out of FT's cybersecurity service line ahead of its 2027 launch Coherence Across Foundations: Act as the technical bridge ensuring DID, Data, and Cybersecurity workstreams are designed as one interoperable stack rather than three siloed engagements, in line with FT's GOAT framework (Governance, Operations, Adoption, Technology) 1.4 Practice Building & Thought Leadership (10%) Mentorship: Guide and upskill a growing team of consultants and analysts across FT's foundations pillar, fostering a culture of technical excellence beyond DID alone Global Presence: Represent Genesis at premier international forums — ID4Africa, World Bank Digital Government and Spring Meetings, and DID/data/cyber developer convenings — publishing high-impact insights and whitepapers that span the foundations stack How This Role Differs From a Pure DID Mandate Anchor specialism: Digital Identity — full ownership, national-scale delivery track record required Contributory remit: Data at Societal Scale and Cybersecurity — working fluency and cross-practice coordination, not delivery ownership Why broadened: Identity is the found

The role involves monitoring project expenditures, preparing cost reports, maintaining cost accounting records, analyzing cost variances, and supporting management with accurate financial information for decision-making. The Cost Accountant works closely with project managers, procurement, warehouse, and finance teams to ensure effective cost control across all company operations. description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Project Context and Scope IOM Ethiopia's vision is to place the rights and well-being of migrants at the centre of its interventions, adopting a preventive, protective, and responsive approach. Its protection interventions in Ethiopia follow a six-pillar intervention that includes direct assistance to migrants, displaced persons and affected communities, thematic guidance, capacity development, advocacy, and research. The Protection Unit (PXU) works closely with the government of Ethiopia and various stakeholders in emergency, displacement, and migration settings to reduce protection risks and address the needs of vulnerable individuals and communities. IOM is guided by rights-based approaches across its migration programming, demonstrating commitment to the safeguarding of vulnerable groups. Within PXU, and under the Migrant Protection and Assistance sub-unit, non-emergency programming areas include Counter-trafficking, Assistance to Vulnerable Migrants (AVM), and Community Outreach. Under the Counter Trafficking interventions, the key areas of engagement include case management to victims of trafficking, developing the capacity of service providers and justice systems, strengthening referral systems and private sector response, supporting the development and implementation of legislation and policies, as well as producing and promoting research and data to improve counter trafficking responses. Under the overall supervision of the Programme Officer (Protection), and direct supervision of the National Officer (Protection), the successful candidate will support the implementation of specialized protection interventions within the Protection Unit, including counter trafficking, case management, capacity development for service provision and referrals for migrants in vulnerable situations, including VoTs, individual protection assistance, and coordination with service providers and relevant authorities to facilitate access to protection services. Additionally, the selected candidate will support the team in trainings and capacity building related to specialized protection, TiP and SoM, and other topics related to provision of assistance to vulnerable migrants. The selected candidate will also be required to provide additional support, as necessary, to other protection teams, including the Return and Reintegration teams, Protection Emergencies, Policy and Liaison, and to coordinate with other programmatic units in the mission.
